source_metadata.title: Cutaneous adverse drug reactions: An 8-year retrospective study on hospitalized patients in Southern China
source_metadata.journal: Indian Journal of Dermatology, Venereology, and Leprology
source_metadata.source_type: Letter to the Editor; retrospective hospital-based study

duplicate_review.finding: No duplicate atoms identified after table-row and narrative overlap review.

consistency_review.finding: Table 2 historical comparison percentages were preserved as reported; the current-period denominator for culprit-drug percentages is not explicitly restated and was not inferred.

extraction_limitations: The source is a short Letter to the Editor with sparse methodological detail.
The source reports dermatologist review and use of a WHO CADR definition but does not describe a formal drug-causality algorithm.
Drug-specific exposure denominators are not reported, so the paper supports proportions among identified CADR cases rather than drug-specific incidence or comparative risk.
The historical comparison uses a previous same-ward study; changes in prescribing, hospitalization thresholds, ascertainment, and case mix may confound temporal comparisons.
The study is retrospective and single-center, limiting causal inference and external validity.
No funding, conflict-of-interest, or data-availability statement is present in the evaluated letter.
Traditional Chinese medicine exposures could not be resolved to specific causative ingredients.
schema_gaps: The LiteratureAtom quantitative_result kind requires an exposures field even for hospital prevalence; hospitalization context was encoded as an exposure and tagged schema_required_exposure_context.

Table 2 reports current and historical percentages but does not explicitly state the denominator for the current-period culprit-drug subset; arm percentages were preserved without inventing denominators.
